content.text: The redline validated. Submitting the finding:

input.quote: (j) This Agreement constitutes the entire Agreement between the parties with respect to its subject matter, and this Agreement supersedes all prior understandings, representations, negotiations and communications between the parties, oral and written.
input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results, and the General Matters provisions (Section 20(a)-(j), p0135-p0149) contain no insurance covenant. Insurance is required here because Garman is not a mere shrink-wrap licensor: under Section 4(a) its personnel deliver and install the Software on our AS400s at each Authorized Location (on-premises work), and under Section 4(b) Garman performs conversion of "Sparkling's data" for future installations, with Section 9(a) requiring us to provide information about our operations and internal procedures. That combination of premises access and data processing is exactly the profile the playbook requires to be insured, and the walk-away position is no insurance for a vendor that processes data or works on our premises. The gap is aggravated because Section 15 limits Garman's liability, so uninsured exposure would sit with us. The obligation runs against the counterparty, so there is no direction problem. Minimal fix: insert a new Section 20(k) after the entire-agreement subsection tracking the model language (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), surviving one year post-term. Fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is flagged in the comment if Garman cannot obtain the preferred limits.

proposal.summary: Insert standard vendor insurance covenant as new Section 20(k)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a standard insurance covenant, as Garman installs Software at our Authorized Locations and converts and accesses our data but carries no insurance obligation anywhere in the Agreement. Our position is CGL of USD 1M/2M, E&O of USD 2M and cyber of USD 5M with certificates on request; we can discuss E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M if the higher limits are unavailable.

ops.text: (k) Garman shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; where Garman processes, stores or has access to Sparkling's data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Garman shall provide certificates of insurance to Sparkling on request.
